result.topic_en: Euler applies his abbreviated difference method: he subtracts successive differences, which grow by the constant 1040, from 6561 and checks the remainders for squares, finding that 85333 and 89293 are prime and setting up the test of 99733.

ubi differentiae per augmentum conſtans $40 \cdot 26 = 1040$ progrediuntur.
Hanc jam poſteriorem reſolutionem maxime ſuccinctam aliquot exemplis illuſtraſſe operae pretium erit.

Exemplum 1.

§. 53. Sumatur $b = 81$ et $a = 1$, ita ut numerus examinandus ſit 85333. Hic ergo differentiae a quadrato $bb = 6561$ continuo ſubtrahendae erunt $40(13 \pm 2)$; $40(39 \pm 2)$; etc. quae creſcunt augmento conſtanti $40 \cdot 26 = 1040$; unde ob ſigna ambigua totus hic calculus per duas columnas abſolvi poterit:

Quoniam igitur nullum reſiduorum ex hac ſubtractione natorum quadratum deprehenditur, tuto concludere poſſumus hunc numerum 85333 eſſe primum.

§. 54. Maneat $b = 81$ ſitque $a = 10$, et numerus examinandus erit $N = 89293$. Hic igitur a quadrato $bb = 6561$ ſubtrahenda erit differentia $40(13 \pm 20)$, ideoque 1320 et $-280$; ſequentes autem differentiae creſcunt augmento $= 1040$. Hinc calculus ita ſe habet:

Quoniam igitur hic etiam nullum quadratum occurrit, numerus propoſitus 89293 certe erit primus.

Exemplum 3.

§. 55. Maneat adhuc $b = 81$ ſumaturque $a = 19$, ut ſit $N = 99733$; et ad examen hujus numeri neceſſe eſt ut a quadrato 6561 ſubtrahantur differentiae augmento 1040 creſcentes, quarum primae ſunt 2040 et $-1000$, hoc modo:

items.english: Since none of the remainders produced by this subtraction is found to be a square, we may safely conclude that this number 85333 is prime.

items.quote: Quoniam igitur hic etiam nullum quadratum occurrit, numerus propoſitus 89293 certe erit primus.
items.english: Since here too no square occurs, the proposed number 89293 will certainly be prime.
